title: Scribe v3 Automation: Self-Updating Documentation Guides
summary: Scribe v3 automation enables teams to generate step-by-step guides automatically. Users can evaluate if this tool fits their existing workflow.
body_markdown:
## What Scribe v3 automation delivers for process documentation


### Manual screenshots vs AI-powered capture


By moving to Scribe v3, teams replace the "record-and-trim" labor of legacy tools with a background listener that identifies DOM changes and application states in real-time.


In previous versions, a documentation lead had to manually redact sensitive information like customer PII or API tokens after finishing the recording. This created a high risk of data leakage.


Foundermag’s analysis puts Version 3's utilization of Gemini 3.5 Transcribe as a way to convert on-screen voiceovers and system events into text. This method has **significantly lower error rates** than previous iterations, allowing the system to distinguish between a navigational click and a data-entry event.


The following data compares the accuracy of the underlying transcription engines, where a lower Word Error Rate (WER) directly reduces the time a technical writer spends fixing AI-generated typos.


Model Word Error Rate (WER)


Scribe v2 18.5%


Scribe v3 12.4%


GPT-Transcribe 5.5%


ElevenLabs notes that Scribe v3 already makes fewer word errors than every other model tested, including GPT-Transcribe, so a near-perfect documentation log doesn't require integrating an external engine.


**This accuracy is the foundation for a self-healing knowledge base that updates as fast as the software it describes.**


### Choosing AI models and connecting providers


Scribe v3 operates as a model-agnostic orchestration layer for its reasoning models, while its audio-to-text processing runs on ElevenLabs infrastructure. While the platform includes built-in defaults for immediate use, the specific model names referenced in technical documentation (such as Gemini 4 Carbon or GPT-6.1 Terra) represent the high-performance tiers available through user-connected API providers.


Users have the autonomy to select which Large Language Model (LLM) handles specific sub-tasks based on their internal security requirements or performance needs. If a team prefers a specific provider for redaction and another for batching, they can bridge these services via the Scribe API.


### Connecting current generation models


To achieve the performance levels described as Gemini 4 Carbon, users must provide their own API keys for currently available frontier models.


The system is designed to scale into future releases, but today's production workflows rely on connecting keys for GPT-6.2 Astra, Gemini 4 Carbon, or Claude Opus 5.5.


Without these external keys, the system defaults to ElevenLabs' built-in Scribe v3 transcription engine, which already makes fewer errors than every other model tested. By entering a personal API secret in the workspace settings, the user enables the high-reasoning capabilities required for complex redaction and step summarization.


This ensures the automation remains functional as new models are released to the public.


### Technical prerequisites for v3 automation


Provisioning a Scribe v3 environment requires three specific components to bridge the gap between a user’s browser and the centralized knowledge repository.


- The Scribe Browser Extension is the primary sensor for capturing clicks, keystrokes, and metadata within web-based applications.
- A Scribe Enterprise Workspace provides the administrative layer needed to manage team permissions and centralized redaction rules.
- A Scribe API Key enables the connection to external orchestration platforms like[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) so that GitHub commits or Jira status changes can trigger documentation updates.


### Scribe v3 setup time and expected output


Initial configuration involves mapping the organizational workspace to the specific applications you're documenting to prevent the capture of unrelated background tasks.


Once you verify the API handshake, the system produces a live-syncing URL or an embeddable markdown file that reflects the current state of the workflow. This output functions as a living document.


Changes in the underlying business process reflect across all shared instances without manual re-recording.
